evidence.description: Boot updater copies APP from 3:/ to dest 0x03000000 via FUN_0006ccf8
File copy routine allocates 0x1000 buffer, reads file, writes to dest, checks bytes-read == file size; no checksum

next_steps: Trace BOOT.bin caller after copy to find actual branch/jump to APP entry
Confirm actual DDR size (via MMIO or about-screen correction) to tighten max APP.bin size estimate
Check runtime heap/stack allocation to refine usable space above 0x03000000
raw_note:
MMU/CP15 decode (BOOT.bin):
- TTBR (c2) set via mcr p15,0,r1, c2,c0,0 at 0x50c with r1=TTBR base = 0x00004000 (DAT_0000286c). Domain register (c3) set to 0x40000000 at 0x514. Control register (c1) read/modified: orr #0x1000 and orr #0x5 then written back at 0x524 (MMU + I-cache enabled). Bit13 was cleared earlier at reset (mrc/bic/mcr at 0x30).
- Page table builder FUN_000027bc fills 1 MB section descriptors: entries 0x000–0x03F use 0xDFE|VA, entries 0x040–0x7FF use 0xDF2|VA (identity). Entries 0x800–0x83F map to (VA index * 1MB + 0x80000000 + 0xDF2) which wraps to low physical (alias of low memory), then 0x840–0xFFF again identity. This yields identity mapping for 0..2 GB and alias window at 0x80000000.
- Conclusion: VA 0x03000000 maps 1:1 to PA 0x03000000; loader assumes >48 MB of RAM despite the 8 MB about-screen readout. Likely DDR is >=64 MB (N3290x supports larger), or the about-screen is misleading.

Entry point: The APP update flow copies APP.bin to 0x03000000 (via FUN_0006ccf8) but jump/handoff is not in this snippet; expected direct branch to 0x03000000 entry after copy.

Size limit: No checksum and no hard-coded cap; limit is contiguous RAM above 0x03000000. If DDR is 64 MB, headroom is ~0x01000000 (16 MB) minus stacks/heaps. Current APP.bin ~2.6 MB well below this. Increase is feasible; verify actual RAM size to set a firm cap.

To do: Trace BOOT handoff to APP (branch target) and confirm runtime RAM size/heap usage for exact maximum.
summary: BOOT enables the MMU with a 1 MB section table at TTBR=0x00004000. The table identity-maps VA 0x00000000–0x7FF00000 (2 GB) with section descriptors 0xDF2/0xDFE and aliases VA 0x80000000–0x83F00000 back to low memory (wrap). Domain register is set to 0x40000000 and control register enables MMU+I-cache. Therefore VA 0x03000000 is mapped 1:1 to PA 0x03000000; the loader assumes physical RAM of at least ~48 MB. APP.bin is copied there by the BOOT flow (in APP update logic) with no checksum. Practical size limit is the RAM remaining above 0x03000000; if DDR is 64 MB, headroom is ~16 MB minus runtime stacks/heaps, so APP can be safely grown well beyond current ~2.6 MB.
title: APP.bin load mechanism and size constraints
